cases.title: Model deviates from trusted reference AND stored inference records fail verification

priority.method: noisy-OR of evidence-group scores (severity x confidence x category weight, +log-volume bonus) + independence bonus per extra Part

cases.rationale: Part 2 reports model-side deviation (dormant_high_influence_unit, identity_mismatch, model_substitution_assessment, parameter_difference, parameter_localized_change, trigger_candidate_response); Part 3 independently reports reinference_mismatch across 3 ledger(s). Recorded outputs are not reproducible by the trusted model, consistent with the served model differing from the trusted one.
cases.next_action: Compare the served model hash with the registry digest; re-run inference with the trusted artifact; hold results produced since the first mismatching record.

cases.title: Stream 'shifted_stream': distribution shift AND provenance failure

priority.method: noisy-OR of evidence-group scores (severity x confidence x category weight, +log-volume bonus) + independence bonus per extra Part

cases.rationale: Part 4 rates the window SEVERE SHIFT (pattern step, onset b2, families geometry) while Part 3 rates the same stream's ledger QUARANTINE. Shift and provenance evidence point at the same window, so the shift cannot be assumed to be a benign environment change.
cases.next_action: Resolve the ledger failure first (Part 3 findings), then re-baseline or investigate the acquisition change.

cases.title: Trigger-like pattern in data AND model-side response

priority.method: noisy-OR of evidence-group scores (severity x confidence x category weight, +log-volume bonus) + independence bonus per extra Part

cases.rationale: Part 1 found recurring localized patterns correlated with a label; Part 2 independently found: 2 Part-1 trigger candidate(s) produced a functional response in the supplied model (attack-success rate up to 1.00). Two independent parts agree. This is a potential trigger/backdoor candidate - not proof of intent or of a functional backdoor beyond the tests executed.
cases.next_action: Quarantine the dataset subset (see pattern support) and the served model; re-run Part 2 against the trusted reference; inspect the top-influence units / patch location.

cases.title: Source 'contributor_x' shows 3 converging data-integrity signals

priority.method: noisy-OR of evidence-group scores (severity x confidence x category weight, +log-volume bonus) + independence bonus per extra Part

cases.rationale: 3 independent Part-1 detectors elevate the same source (duplicate rate, label_anomaly rate, trigger_candidate rate; 128 samples, cross-signal count 3). Evidence concentrates in one contributor rather than being spread across the dataset.
cases.next_action: Inspect duplicate/trigger groups and label-anomaly samples attributed to 'contributor_x'; check contributor provenance before allowing this data into training.

cases.next_action: Inspect the listed samples/assets; look for corroborating signal in another Part before escalating.

assumptions: Part 3/4 findings linked to the single supplied Part 2 model (MODEL-trojan_checker) as the served model

reproducibility.rerun: python -m cv_assurance part5 assemble --results <same dirs> --out <dir> [--policy <same policy>] -> identical case_ids and evidence_hashes

limitations: Rule-based correlation only: converging evidence raises review priority, it does not establish intent, attribution or a functional backdoor beyond tests executed.
The review-priority score is a transparent noisy-OR of policy weights, not a probability of malicious activity.
Absence of findings is not proof of safety; UNAVAILABLE items are coverage gaps, never passes.
A distribution shift is not automatically an attack; governance decides whether it is acceptable.
The audit trail is tamper-evident within the declared trust boundary; a fully privileged attacker who controls the host, the key or the assurance binary is out of scope.
Inputs are trusted only from the point at which Parts 1-4 artifacts were captured (their hashes are recorded here).
honest_claims: Detects specified integrity inconsistencies and controlled attack scenarios and correlates them across data, model, inference and shift.
Every case links to raw findings, their detector versions and the hash of the artifact that produced them.
Runs offline; no retraining, no cloud/API calls; unavailable tests are disclosed.
